title: Guard this repository's TypeScript against Bun's silent declare strip
description: Bun 1.3.14 strips a top-level binding named declare in a .ts file as if it were a TypeScript ambient declaration: the definition and every bare-identifier call to it vanish with no diagnostic and exit 0. Found while writing WCLI-9's tests, where a helper named declare silently did nothing and the resulting failures pointed at the code under test rather than at the helper. A test helper that silently does not run is worse than one that fails: a security assertion behind it can pass vacuously. Reproduction: a file containing 'function declare(value: string): void { console.log("ran", value); } declare("hello");' prints nothing under bun, prints normally with the same content as .js, and is unaffected when the function is named anything else; 'const declare = () => {}' with 'declare()' behaves the same way, while a member call such as holder.declare() is unaffected. The guard belongs in this repository because its whole test suite is Bun-run TypeScript; the upstream report is the operator's to route.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A repository check fails, with the offending file and line named, when any tracked .ts file declares a top-level binding named declare or calls it as a bare identifier
The guard is proven both ways: it reports a deliberate case in a test fixture, and it passes on the current tree
The check runs as part of bun run check rather than as a separate command nobody runs
